subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures what is happening in a space without asking anyone.

subsystems.name: Interoperability layer
subsystems.role: lets lights, blinds, heating and appliances from different makers be controlled through one interface.
parts: building protocols such as BACnet or KNX

subsystems.name: Context and intent engine
subsystems.role: turns raw sensor streams into an estimate of who is present, what they are doing and what they probably want.

subsystems.name: Actuation and control
subsystems.role: changes the physical environment — typically heating, cooling, light and shade.

subsystems.name: Identity and personalisation
subsystems.role: decides whose preferences win when two people share a room.

subsystems.name: BCI input channel
subsystems.role: an optional, still-experimental route for inferring intent directly from brain signals.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the building
buildSteps.detail: Radar, CO₂ and thermal sensors are fitted per room at heights that see occupants but not through walls, plus metering on major loads.

buildSteps.title: Unify the device layer
buildSteps.detail: Devices are commissioned onto one standard so the control software sees them as capabilities (light, heat, shade) rather than brands.

buildSteps.title: Collect labelled data
buildSteps.detail: For months, sensor traces are recorded alongside what occupants actually did — which window they opened, which setpoint they chose.

buildSteps.title: Train models
buildSteps.detail: Activity and comfort models learn patterns such as CO₂ rising while a room fills, or a person preferring 21 °C while working but 19 °C while sleeping.

buildSteps.title: Run inference at the edge
buildSteps.detail: Models are quantised to run on a local hub in tens of milliseconds, so control still works without internet and video never leaves the home.

buildSteps.title: Close the control loop
buildSteps.detail: The system adjusts heating, lighting and shading automatically, with an override that teaches it when it guessed wrong.

buildSteps.title: Add identity and personalisation
buildSteps.detail: Individual preferences are attached to profiles and merged with a fair rule when people disagree.

buildSteps.title: Pilot a BCI channel
buildSteps.detail: In a research setting only, a small headset is worn for calibration sessions; the classifier is trained on labelled mental states and tested as an extra input, never the only one.

buildSteps.title: Audit privacy
buildSteps.detail: Data minimisation, local storage and a visible indicator of when sensing is active are built in from the start, because a system that guesses intent is also a surveillance system.

prerequisites.why: radar and gas sensors now cost a few dollars each and can run for years on a coin cell.
Matter and Thread cover common devices, but HVAC plant and older building systems often remain proprietary.
occupancy is fairly well solved; inferring what a person wants next is not.
electrodes on the scalp pick up faint, noisy signals; today's systems need calibration and can decode a handful of commands, not unspoken intent.
privacy and latency both require inference locally rather than in the cloud.

pathway.milestone: sensor-rich buildings that dim lights and trim heating when rooms are empty
pathway.unlocks: meaningful energy savings with no user input.

pathway.milestone: per-person comfort control driven by phones and wearables
pathway.unlocks: comfort settings that follow a person between rooms rather than rooms that guess.

pathway.milestone: passive BCI as an accessibility input, for people who cannot use voice or touch
pathway.unlocks: real-world validation of EEG decoding outside the lab and honest limits on what it can read.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop environments that anticipate actions across a district
pathway.unlocks: an ambient layer only if consent, identity and failure modes are solved — otherwise it stays a well-automated building.
